It thus belongs to gastroenterology/medical imaging with reinforcement learning implemented via deep actor-critic and Q-network methods.

rationale: The paper develops a deep graph contrastive learning framework (hierarchical graph attention encoder with hard negative mining) applied to fMRI functional connectome fingerprinting, with a supervised psychiatric disorder classification task for transfer evaluation. Core domains are medical imaging/machine learning, with self-supervised contrastive (representation) learning as the main training paradigm.

The paper develops a ZVO/carbon-cloth electrochemical sensor for pesticide residues and applies machine learning to classify pesticides and predict concentrations from overlapping sensor signals. Specific ML algorithms are not named, so only the supervised learning paradigm (classification plus concentration regression) can be reliably tagged.

The paper applies AlphaFold 3, a deep learning structure-prediction model, within a structure-guided computational workflow to design DNA tweezer nanostructures targeting glioblastoma biomarkers S100A4 and midkine, followed by HDOCK molecular docking. The subject is structural bioinformatics/biomarker biosensor design rather than method development, so deep learning is the only model family evidenced.

This is a randomized controlled trial evaluating Endo-Wing versus transparent tip hoods for colonoscopy combined with linked color imaging and a computer-aided detection (CADe) system for adenoma detection. The clinical subject is gastrointestinal endoscopy with medical imaging support, and the only AI element is the CADe application, whose underlying learning algorithm or paradigm is not described in the abstract.

The paper develops a self-supervised deep learning reconstruction framework (SS-4DMRF) for 4D MRI fingerprinting in liver cancer radiotherapy, built around Swin Transformer blocks in a physics-informed pattern matching network and a low-rank-constrained registration network. Because self-supervision uses no labels and no explicit supervised/semi-supervised/reinforcement signal, it is best captured under the unsupervised paradigm with the deep learning family.

The study applies unsupervised LDA topic modeling to 39,548 home health care publications, mapping research themes in the health services literature. It is a text-mining/NLP study with a public health and health services focus, using no deep learning or supervised methods.

The paper develops a deep learning framework for webly supervised fine-grained image recognition that fine-tunes a foundation model encoder using LoRA, applies bilinear global-local feature fusion, and employs a noise-aware supervised contrastive loss, making deep learning, representation learning, and transfer learning the salient model families. No biomedical domain is evident from the abstract, so only Computer science/Machine learning domains apply.

Domains reflect multi-omics integration (genomics/transcriptomics/epigenomics layers) with bioinformatics and machine learning as core subjects.

The paper applies AI-based computational tools specifically via AlphaFold deep learning structure modeling to predict how rare ACVR1 variants disrupt protein interactions, within a whole-genome sequencing rare variant study of juvenile idi arthritis pedigrees. The paper compares NLP approaches (rule-based regular expressions, TF-IDF with logistic regression, and BERT) to extract molecular markers (IDH, ATRX) from glioma pathology reports, a supervised clinical text-mining task in medical informatics. All three approaches are trained/evaluated on labelled data, so supervised learning is the paradigm.

The paper develops and validates a supervised text-classification system for detecting self-harm in ED triage notes, using extensive text normalisation plus a classifier built on 1931 selected features, indicating a classical feature-based ML approach. The domains reflect clinical medicine applied through NLP and medical informatics, with no specific named model type given in the abstract.

The paper develops supervised classifiers (Bayesian neural networks built on feedforward networks) for eight-class tissue identification from bioimpedance features, with a stacking ensemble as meta-learner and temperature scaling for calibration. The application is biomedical sensing/tissue classification, so Biomedical science and Machine learning are the applicable domain terms.

The paper develops a supervised deep learning model (PGMA-Net) with attention-based pathology-prior guidance for classifying oral squamous cell carcinoma pathological images, using domain adaptation for multi-center generalization. Its subject is head and neck cancer diagnosis via pathology image analysis.

An epidemiological survey study (NHANES/KNHANES) of cardiorenal anemia syndrome using lasso for predictor selection and CatBoost for prediction with SHAP interpretation; the ML component is supervised classical machine learning.

The paper develops a supervised deep learning classifier predicting protein complex symmetry from single sequences, combining persistent GLMY homology-derived topological features with the pretrained ESM2 protein language model. The study applies Latent Class Growth Analysis (LCGA), an unsupervised latent class mixture method, to identify household-chaos trajectories, plus ANOVA/ANCOVA for outcome comparisons. The study applies integrative bioinformatics to gastric cancer transcriptomics, using unsupervised clustering of scRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq data to define molecular subtypes, cell death patterns, and prognostic biomarkers. The paper develops a deep learning-based anomaly detection system for healthcare IoT security with severity estimation (supervised deep learning), plus a reinforcement learning component (Q-Score-based checkpoint selection) within a post-quantum-verified rollback framework.

CausalBGM is a Bayesian generative modeling framework that learns individual-specific latent confounder representations to estimate treatment effects with posterior intervals, a statistical/AI methodology paper rather than a domain-application study. The study applies a pretrained multimodal generative model (Stable Diffusion, a latent diffusion model) to extract and analyze latent representations of artworks, an unsupervised use of a deep generative model. The paper develops a supervised deep learning object detector (YOLOv11-based) for flame detection in UAV aerial imagery, using convolutional components with deformable convolutions, variance-aware attention, and an MPDIoU loss. The subject is computer vision/machine learning applied to image analysis rather than a biomedical or omics domain.

A retrospective cohort study applying multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic splines to predict incident cardiovascular disease in rectal cancer survivors, using a biomarker index (CTI) as a supervised predictor. No neural, ensemble, or unsupervised methods are described beyond classical regression-based modelling and performance evaluation.

The study identifies distinct academic/athletic identity profiles among student-athletes by clustering individuals on self-report measures, which corresponds to latent profile analysis, an unsupervised person-centered classification method. The domain is genomic sequence analysis (splice site/gene structure prediction), fitting computational biology, bioinformatics, and machine learning.

The study applies multi-omics/transcriptomic bioinformatics (eRNA-associated signatures in OA and T2DM) using WGCNA co-expression network analysis (unsupervised) and CIBERSORT-based immune cell deconvolution, both classical non-deep methods, rather than developing a new AI model.

The study is a clinical epidemiology/methodology paper empirically comparing seven continuous-predictor modelling approaches (linear/quadratic terms, restricted cubic splines, fractional polynomials, dichotomisation, tertiles, XGBoost) for supervised clinical prediction stability, using classical statistical/ML methods on emergency department data.

The paper uses a panel of LLMs (including DeepSeek) with counterfactual synthetic patient profiles to audit and mitigate socioeconomic bias in physical-activity prescriptions, situating it in public health with an AI/LLM evaluation methodology. A biomedical data descriptor providing pixel-level annotated OCT images for macular hole surgery outcomes, situating it in ophthalmic medical imaging. The reference baseline is nnUNet, a supervised U-Net-style deep learning segmentation model trained on expert-validated masks.

Model performance evaluation (AUC, calibration, bootstrap validation) confirms a predictive modeling rather than mechanistic study.

The study uses unsupervised k-means clustering on clinical/biochemical variables to identify CSA phenotypes, then supervised adaptive LASSO and multivariable logistic regression for phenotype-specific determinants. The subject is cardiology (coronary spastic angina) with patient phenotyping.

The paper applies single-cell RNA-seq analysis to build a CNS immune cell atlas for rabies-infected mice, an inherently unsupervised workflow of dimensionality reduction and cell clustering rather than a named deep learning model. The study applies a supervised gradient boosting model to estimate propensity scores for matching in a target trial emulation of post-hospital discharge pathways in older multimorbid patients. The paper develops an LLM-based NLP framework, validated against predefined labels, to extract decision reasons from participants' free-text verbal reports, indicating supervised use of large language models for text classification. The subject matter is computational/behavioral decision science with the core methodological contribution lying in NLP and machine learning.

The paper develops a supervised, alignment-free pipeline (DeltaFold Classifier) that encodes protein 3D structures via persistent homology (Biotopological Markers) and trains machine learning models for SCOP/CATH hierarchical structure classification. The specific classifier family is not named, so only the supervised classical-ML framing is tagged.

The study applies k-means clustering to derive exploratory spinopelvic compensation patterns and ridge-penalized logistic regression for baseline and contemporaneous prediction of a composite MCID endpoint after total knee arthroplasty. The subject domain is orthopedic/musculoskeletal clinical outcome research, with no deeper EDAM tier-3 term applicable.

The paper develops a physics-informed deep learning motion-correction network for dynamic wrist 4DCT, trained in a supervised manner with paired simulated motion-corrupted/static ground-truth images. The work sits in medical imaging physics (CT simulation, forward projection and reconstruction), so Physics/Imaging/Medical imaging and Tomography are the appropriate domain tags.

The paper compares ARIMA (classical statistical time-series method), an artificial neural network, and a hybrid ARIMA-ANN for forecasting Somalia's infant mortality rate, a public health indicator. ARIMA maps to classical machine learning, the ANN to a classic (non-deep) neural network, and the task is supervised time-series forecasting.

The paper benchmarks five LLMs for extracting structured clinical variables from Portuguese EHR notes against human-annotated labels, placing it in medical informatics/NLP. The models are evaluated in a supervised benchmarking setup against a manually curated dataset, and each tested LLM is tagged verbatim.

The study uses machine-learning prioritisation of cross-disease shared genes as candidate biomarkers, evaluated by ROC AUC in independent datasets, which is a supervised classical ML workflow, though the specific algorithm is not named in the abstract. The subject matter is immunometabolic comorbidity (RA and MASLD) centred on a macrophage-polarisation gene signature.

The clinical application is noninvasive neuromonitoring in acute ischemic stroke, situating it in neurology and medical imaging.

The paper develops a prognostic risk and survival prediction tool for resected NSCLC patients using a Cox proportional hazards regression model on clinicopathological features, implemented as freely accessible software. This is a supervised classical statistical learning approach applied in the oncology/medical informatics domain.

The paper develops hierarchical recurrent deep neural network models with top-down modulatory feedback to study audiovisual integration, making deep learning the core model family trained on a task (supervised-style training implied by the audiovisual integration task). The paper records monkey IT (area TE) neuronal responses to faces and compares representations with deep vision models, so the core domain is neurobiology with machine learning as a secondary domain. The paper develops a supervised radiomics nomogram using LASSO for feature selection and logistic regression for prediction of extrathyroidal extension in papillary thyroid carcinoma, with no neural or deep learning components.

The paper refactors DL_FFLUX, a machine learning potential combining quantum chemical topology with supervised ML (FFLUX potentials are built from Gaussian process/kriging regression on quantum chemical data) for molecular dynamics simulations. The work sits in computational chemistry and molecular simulation, focusing on performance optimization rather than a new learning architecture.

The paper develops a supervised deep learning model (Mixture-of-Experts with a gating network) for interpretable Alzheimer's diagnosis from multimodal neuroimaging (MRI, amyloid PET) and demographic data, placing it in medicine/medical informatics with medical imaging as the data domain.

The paper applies supervised classification of EEG-derived features (source-localized wPLI connectivity and microstates) for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis, so supervised learning is the only defensible paradigm. No specific model family or algorithm is named in the abstract, so model_family and model_type are left empty.

The study integrates public mRNA/miRNA and single-cell transcriptomic datasets to prioritize miRNA regulators of fibrotic-immune remodeling in ligamentum flavum hypertrophy, using enrichment, PPI network, and database-driven analyses. The only AI/ML component is LASSO regression used to prioritize hub gene features, which is supervised classical machine learning.

The study applies scRNA-seq and intercellular communication analysis to study radiation cystitis in the bladder, with pharmacological evaluation of Icariside II. The paper develops a supervised deep learning radiomics framework for coronary CTA/CT-FFR analysis to identify high-risk plaques and predict MACE, using U-Net for coronary segmentation and a CNN+Transformer multimodal fusion model, placing it squarely in cardiology and medical imaging (CT tomography).

The paper develops a physics-feature-fused data-driven framework using a three-input feedforward artificial neural network trained on labelled (simulated) damage states with known targets, i.e. supervised shallow neural network learning. Since the application is structural health monitoring of composites rather than a biomedical subject, only the computer science/machine learning domain tiers apply.

The paper develops supervised feedforward multilayer-perceptron neural networks (trained via Levenberg-Marquardt and scaled conjugate gradient) to predict CO2 solubility in ionic liquids, a chemistry/computational chemistry task; the plain MLP is best classed as a classic neural network rather than deep learning, and no other model families or tier-3 topics apply.

The paper develops a deep learning framework built on a theoretically guaranteed isometric autoencoder that reconstructs the free-energy landscape of biomacromolecules from cryo-EM data, an unsupervised representation-learning task applied to 50S ribosome and SARS-CoV-2 spike protein datasets.

The paper analyzes evolutionary constraint (GERP scores) and deleterious/hypervariable load in a tetraploid potato breeding panel and uses load features in genomic prediction of trait phenotypes such as yield. Genomic prediction is a supervised regression/classification task typically implemented with classical statistical ML methods, though no specific model family is named in the abstract.

The paper develops a framework that integrates locally deployed large language models with personal knowledge bases and bioinformatics tools into an autonomous multi-component system for research workflows. No training paradigm is described, so learning_paradigm is empty.

A retrospective cohort study building a supervised prognostic nomogram for adjacent segment disease after anterior cervical spine surgery, using LASSO for feature selection and multivariable logistic regression for prediction, both classical machine learning methods.

The paper applies unsupervised clustering (a classical ML technique) to allergen-specific IgE multiplex serology data from dogs to identify molecular sensitization profiles in a veterinary allergy context. The paper integrates transcriptomic and proteomic omics data in watermelon to model seed vigor, using machine-learning-based proteomic predictors (a supervised quantitative prediction task) and a constructed regulatory network; the abstract does not specify a particular algorithm, so the model type is tagged verbatim.

The paper builds supervised QSAR-style models (multiple linear regression and ordinal classification) using biomimetic chromatographic descriptors to predict drug-induced phospholipidosis liability, a toxicological safety concern in medicinal chemistry/drug development.
